headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Airbyte can move business data into a write-capable RAG course environment that handles secrets and external APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes API-driven data flows and broad network egress, while the course agent reads files, runs shells, and uses stdin/stdout in a local development environment. No shared clipboard or MCP is documented, so the bridge is indirect; prompt injection is possible only if Airbyte-fed content is later copied into the course agent’s inputs.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is manually pasted into the course agent's stdin/stdout prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF the course agent is configured to treat imported text as instructions, malicious content can steer it.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs out of prompt text; pass only structured fields.
Add a manual review step before any copy-paste into the course agent.
Prefix imported content with a fixed delimiter and instruction to ignore embedded commands.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between pipeline outputs and prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; the course agent touches configuration secrets and can write/read the filesystem. A shared workspace is not stated, so leakage is inferred rather than proven, but if Airbyte exports data into files the course agent can read, sensitive material could flow into its outputs or external API calls.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into a directory readable by the course agent, leakage becomes possible.
IF the course agent sends retrieved files to external APIs, secrets or business data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store Airbyte exports in a separate directory with restrictive permissions.
Remove secrets from any shared export path before the course agent reads it.
Disable outbound API calls for the course agent during shared-data runs.
Use a throwaway workspace for each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has API access and broad egress, while the course agent can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, install packages, and write the filesystem. Even without explicit shared-state documentation, overlapping write-adjacent capabilities create a realistic conflict if both operate on the same workspace or downstream resources.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path, concurrent writes can clobber outputs.
IF both agents mutate the same external dataset or API-backed resource, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use file locks or a single-writer convention.
Snapshot outputs before the second agent runs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce business data that the course agent may ingest through files or APIs, and the course agent is capable of acting on that input with shell and network tools. Because no verification step is documented, erroneous or malformed upstream output can cascade into downstream actions or generated content.
conditions: IF the course agent treats Airbyte-produced records as authoritative, upstream errors propagate downstream.
IF the course agent automates actions from those records, a bad record can trigger incorrect side effects.
mitigations: Require a validation step before the course agent consumes Airbyte output.
Compare sampled records against the source system.
Log and reject malformed rows before downstream use.
Limit the course agent to read-only analysis for first-pass runs.
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data, while the course agent handles academic papers plus configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment with external API surfaces. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if business data is routed into the course agent’s secret-bearing workflow or third-party APIs.
conditions: IF business data is routed through the course agent's external API calls, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF secrets and business data share the same workspace, handling policies can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated business data out of the course agent workspace.
Separate secret-bearing files from data-processing files.
Review API retention settings before any run.
Document the data classes allowed in each agent.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
